post.title: Consistent Hashing
post.subtitle: Learn how consistent hashing minimizes cache misses during horizontal scaling and node failures.
post.brief:
Consistent hashing is a scaling pattern where both database/cache nodes and data keys are mapped onto a circular hash ring.
This limits the number of keys remapped when nodes are added or removed to K

## Scenario context

Multi-tier caching and replicated storage pipeline ensuring fast reads and transactional consistency.
The system topology organizes components across groups: Application Workers, Volatile Memory Tier, Persistent Disk Tier. Each component maintains isolated responsibilities to protect system throughput.

This walkthrough focuses on **Component Topology & Roles**.

Before making a design choice, clarify:

- The system topology organizes components across groups: Application Workers, Volatile Memory Tier, Persistent Disk Tier.
- Each component maintains isolated responsibilities to protect system throughput.

**Concepts in play:** caching, load-balancing, consistency-replication, hash-tables-and-bloom-filters

## Stage 1 — Data Flow & Inter-Service Invariants

- In-memory caching handles high-frequency read spikes, reserving disk transactions strictly for state modifications.
